FAUSTINO P. TAN Office of the Secretary to the Sanggunian Municipality of Don Marcelino Province of Davao Occidental Dear Mr. Tan: We refer to your earlier letter dated April 8, 2024 requesting for guidance on local legislative process, specifically on the matter of certifying the urgency of a proposed measure. Your request for guidance stemmed from the recent Congressional hearing involving some municipal officials of San Simon, Pampanga. According to you, during the hearing, Congressman Johnny T. Pimentel of the 2nd District of Surigao del Sur emphasized that there must be a prior letter request from the Office of the Mayor, addressed to the Sangguniang Bayan to certify a certain measure as urgent, without which the latter has no basis in certifying the same as urgent for its immediate deliberation. Based on the foregoing representations, the following queries are proferred: 1. It is correct to assume that based on the provisions of RA 7160 the power to call for a special session is conferred to both the mayor or to the majority of the Sangguniang Bayan members and corollary to such power, both the former and the latter also share similar implied discretionary power to certify a certain measure as urgent? 2. If the answer to the first query is in the affirmative, can it be safely inferred that the aforenamed lawmaker could be mistaken on his assertion that, without the letter request of the Mayor for the Sangguniang Bayan to certify the measure as urgent, the latter has no justifiable basis to consider the measure as urgent for their immediate deliberation? 3. Granting without conceding that the letter request of the Mayor to certify a certain measure as urgent is a prerequisite, can the latter be always obligated to seek the letter request of the former to certify certain measure as urgent for it to be immediately deliberated upon by the latter in the plenary session? 4. Can the implied power of the majority of the SB Members to certify a certain measure as urgent be only exercised when calling for a special session? What about during the conduct of a regular session, can the Sanggunian validly "Matino, Mahusay at Maaasahan" Trunkline No. (02) 8876 3454

exercise its implied power to decide through the majority votes to certify the urgency of a proposed measure? Worthy of an example is the matter of deciding the urgency of plain resolution of sympathy to the bereaved family of a deceased official or a prominent person? For purposes of clarity, we deem it apt to compartmentalize the issues and render our opinion in the following manner. The Local Chief Executive (LCE) and a Majority of the Members of the Sanggunian have Concurrent Authority to Call Special Sessions May we apprise you that Section 52(b) of the Local Government Code of 1991 (LGC) 1 specifically identifies who can call special sessions of the Sanggunian, viz: Section 52. Sessions. - Xxx (b) When public interest so demands, special sessions may be called bv the local chief executive or by a maiority of the members of the sanqqunian. [Emphasis suppliedl From the foregoing, it is clear that the LGC grants concurrent authority to the LCE and a majority of the members of the sanggunian to call special sessions, when public interest so requires. The Authority to Certify as Urgent Any Legislative Item is Reserved to the Local Chief Executive Foremost, the LCE has the duty to address the Sanggunian at the opening of the regular session or as may be deemed necessary to communicate to them the priority policies and programs of the LGU. Section 444 of the LGC provides: Section 444. The Chief Executive: Powers, Duties, Functions and Compensation. — (b) For efficient, effective and economical govemance the purpose of which is the general welfare of the municipality and its inhabitants pursuant to Section 16 of this Code, the municipal mayor shall: (1) Exercise general supervision and control over all programs, projects, services, and activities of the municipal government, and in this connection, shall: (iii) At the opening of the regular session of the sangguniang bayan for every calendar year and, as may be deemed necessary, present the program of govemment and propose policies and projects for the consideration of the sangguniang bayan as the general welfare of the inhabitants and the needs of the municipal government may require; Correspondingly, the Implementing Rules and Regulations of the LGC also recognized the power of the LCE to determine what matters will be considered as urgent. Article 107 provides: Republic Act No. 7160 Page 2 of 3

ARTICLE 107. Ordinances and Resolutions. — Tho following rules shall govern the enactmont of ordinancos and rosolutions, Xxx (e) Any legislative tnattor duly codifiod by tho local chiol oxocutivo os urgent, whether or not it is includod in tho calondar businoss, may bo presented and considomd by tho body at tho samo mooting Without need of suspending the tulos. Further, in DILG Opinion. No. 27, s. 2009, this Department said. "The LGC recognizes the competence of the local chiolexocutive to certify as urgent any ordinance or resolution to be passed by the sanggunian. However, the LGC and its IRR failed to categorically specify as to what ordinances and/or resolutions should be certified as urgent. Neither is there any fixed measure or, at the very least, any instance or controlling condition that will give rise to the certification as urgent any passage of an ordinance or resolution. The authoritv vested upon a local chief executive certifying as urgent an le islative matter is ranted b lawin order to allow the LGUs at the instance of the local chief executive. to respond quickly. through leqislative measures, any exigencv of public service. public emerqencyz or calamity which requires immediate attention and solution. xxx From the foregoing, it is clear that it is the LCE who is vested with the authority to certify legislative matters as urgent, and the Sanggunian cannot exercise this power. Such authority arose from the duty imposed upon the LCE to determine the programs or projects that will be beneficial and advantageous to the local government unit. The LCE's authority to certify legislative matters as urgent allows LGUs to respond quickly to public emergencies, calamities, or other public service needs. Accordingly, we are of the opinion that the Sanggunian may not consider a legislative matter as urgent unless it is certified as such by the LCE. When certified, it shall have priority over all other items of business, and shall be considered without need of suspending the rules or even if it is not included in the business of the day. The opinion of this Department is based solely on the facts and representations you have narrated in your letter and our appreciation of the same. Further, this opinion is being rendered without prejudice to any contrary opinion of competent authorities and the courts. We hope to have addressed your concern accordingly. Thank you. Very truly yours, BY AUTHORITY OF THE SECRETARY: ATTY. ROMEO P. BENITEZ Undersecretary for External, Legal and Legislative Affairs OUSELLNRPB/LLLS-LRALLD/jvpr Page 3 of3
